title: Triage remaining code scanning alerts after LLM and audit fixes
description:
After the LLM base-URL fix bundle and the blunder-audit hardening work, 16 open code-scanning alerts remain. These should be handled as a single follow-up triage issue with a bias toward small real fixes before dismissing alerts.

Expected remaining buckets:
- `java/implicit-cast-in-compound-assignment` alerts 29-35 in `Mage.Client`, `Mage.Sets`, and `Mage`. These look like explicit-cast cleanup, not security bugs. If the arithmetic intent is obvious, fixing them mechanically may be cheaper than carrying dismissals.
- `py/bind-socket-all-network-interfaces` alerts 10-14 in `puppeteer/src/puppeteer/port.py`, `scripts/analysis/blunder_audit.py`, and `puppeteer/tests/test_port.py`. Some of these are likely local-only false positives, but the fixes may be simple: bind probes to `127.0.0.1` instead of `""` where that still preserves behavior, and dismiss the rest if the all-interface bind is intentional.
- `js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization` alerts 38-39 in `website/src/scripts/game-renderer.js`. These currently appear to be false positives because the cleaned strings flow into `textContent` / `createTextNode`, not HTML sinks.
- `js/incomplete-url-scheme-check` alert 1 in `website/tests/e2e/links.test.js`. This is test code and probably a trivial fix by rejecting `data:` and `vbscript:` alongside the existing schemes.
- `py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` alert 19 in `puppeteer/tests/test_youtube.py`. This is also test-only and likely should be dismissed unless there is an equally small cleanup.

Suggested outcome:
- Implement any low-noise code fixes that are obviously correct.
- Dismiss only the alerts that are clearly test-only or false positives, with concise notes explaining the sink / threat model.
- Keep this separate from the higher-signal security fixes so the PR history does not mix real hardening with scanner cleanup.
